proof_attempt_summary: Proved a leverage-only admissibility threshold for design-stage use of an external prognostic score: gamma(S) = min{lambda_max(K|H_n) : K1=0, diag K = diag P_S} equals a one-dimensional feasibility search U(diag P_S), via a Gram completion whose existence is the polygon inequality on the square-root diagonal slack; S is admissible iff gamma(S) < 1, and then rho*(S) = sqrt(gamma(S)) >= sqrt(dim(S)/(n-1)). Nothing collapsed — the run was stopped at F2 by operator decision once the projected paper score fell below the 7.5 bar. What remains is delivery, not mathematics: quantify the improvement above the threshold for general S, close the p/(n-1) regret slack (worst at rank-one S), and replace the exponential kappa(S) enumeration with a score-matrix-computable object. Revive via a field->field `--upgrade ... --upgrade-axis computation`, not a cold restart.
tldr: An external prognostic score can improve design only when the fixed potential-outcome mean vector is sufficiently aligned with the centered score subspace; the realized alignment \(\rho_{\mu}(S)=\|P_S\mu\|_2/\|\mu\|_2\) is not observable at the design stage, and \(\rho\) is a free oracle lower-bound index rather than a score-matrix functional. For an arbitrary score subspace, the paper gives an exact finite, generally exponential saddle program for the minimax SATE risk over every balanced mean-zero assignment law, with an attaining sign-pair mixture and a matching full-class converse. Its main closed-form result is the leverage-only frontier \(\gamma(S)=U(\operatorname{diag}(P_S))\), so \(S\) is admissible exactly when \(\gamma(S)<1\), and then \(\rho^*(S)=\sqrt{\gamma(S)}\); this threshold is computed from the score matrix by a one-dimensional feasibility search. Exact closed forms are also obtained for unequal two-block spaces and homogeneous even-block spaces, with matched pairs as the block-size-two specialization. For a single design chosen without knowing \(\rho\), the exact finite regret is given by a generally exponential robust program and obeys the universal normalized bracket \[\frac{p}{n-1}\{c_n-\kappa(S)\}\leq\frac{n}{4M}R^*(n,S)\leq c_n-\kappa(S).\] Complete randomization witnesses the upper bound, and homogeneous even-block spaces attain the lower bound.
gap: Existing design theory either proves that complete randomization is minimax without predictive structure, optimizes a named restricted design under a chosen tuning parameter, or defines a generic mixed-strategy criterion and evaluates ellipsoidal outcome classes. It does not solve the nonellipsoidal lower score-energy shell, determine its exact fixed-count realizable covariance, or locate the transition below perfect prediction for an arbitrary external-score subspace.
fill: The proposal combines a rank-one-exact semidefinite adversary, minimax duality over balanced sign mixtures, and a compressed spectral certificate to deliver the value, attaining design, converse, admissibility dichotomy, and critical quality using only the score geometry available before randomization.
